streak_assessment: Scientific non-improvements since the newest promotion (exp-0089, the accepted 3 cp/square net-mobility leaf term, score 0.625) stand at exactly one: exp-0090's non-linear quadratic king-danger term returned an inconclusive paired arena (0.508, CI [0.436, 0.580]), with clean CI, reliability and ablation gates and zero agent failures. That is 1 of the required 5 consecutive non-improvements, so the numeric stop threshold is not met. More importantly, the qualitative test also fails: the search / move-ordering / quiescence / time-management direction is genuinely saturated in its tested form (exp-0076..exp-0088 plateau, and every family in the handoff's exhausted list has been tried), but the active direction is leaf evaluation, which exp-0089 only just opened and which remains largely unexplored — of the standard positional terms, only mobility (accepted) and non-linear king danger (inconclusive) have reached the arena, while passed pawns, rook-on-open-file and the bishop pair have never been tried. exp-0089 is direct proof that a single cheap hand-scaled leaf term can move the paired-arena score to 0.625 without retraining, so this direction is far from exhausted. The prior audit's guardrails explicitly pre-authorised passed pawns as the next distinct term if the king-danger arena came back inconclusive, which is exactly what happened. Decision is clearly CONTINUE.
recurring_failure_modes: Non-forced threefold-repetition draws from balanced-or-better positions are the dominant failure mode: 29 of 64 games ended by threefold repetition, and the PGNs show the engine reaching equal or materially favourable middlegames/endgames and then shuffling pieces with no plan (e.g. exp-0090 game 1 Bc7/Bd8 rook-ending shuffle with an extra passed b-pawn; game 8 Reti rook ending with extra pawns Rb8/Rb3/Rc6 repetition; several Nb4/Na2, Rc6/Rd6, Bc5/Be1 oscillations). The accepted mobility term reduced but did not remove this: in locked or simplified positions net mobility is nearly constant across candidate moves, so alpha-beta still has no gradient toward the one kind of progress that matters there — advancing a passed or majority pawn.

Every single one of the 17 losses is a checkmate (loss_breakdown is all 'checkmate', 8 white / 9 black). They span a middlegame king hunt against an uncastled king and multiple long (50-90 move) queen/rook endgame king hunts. exp-0090 targeted this column directly with a quadratic king-danger term and did not move the score, suggesting the mate losses are downstream of poor endgame conversion and passive defence rather than a missing static king-attack scalar.

Endgame conversion / technique is weak: the engine repeatedly fails to convert extra material or a passed pawn, and repeatedly fails to make progress in won or drawn rook endings, which is what feeds both the repetition draws and, when it drifts, the king-hunt losses.

No passed-pawn awareness anywhere in the evaluator: _model_evaluate is tapered PSQT + net mobility + a flat castling scalar, with nothing that rewards pawn advancement or promotion threats, so the search cannot distinguish a 7th-rank passer from a 2nd-rank pawn beyond the raw PSQT value.

next_direction.title: Passed-pawn advancement term in the leaf evaluation
next_direction.hypothesis: Adding a cheap rank-scaled passed-pawn bonus to _model_evaluate gives alpha-beta a monotone progress gradient in simplified and locked positions that mobility cannot express, converting some of the balanced-or-better threefold-repetition draws into wins and improving conversion of favourable endgames without retraining. At import, precompute two 64-entry tuples of plain-int bitboards, _PASSED_MASK_WHITE/_PASSED_MASK_BLACK, where entry s is the union of the pawn's file and both adjacent files restricted to the ranks strictly ahead of s toward promotion (built from chess.BB_FILES / chess.square_rank / chess.square_file). In _model_evaluate, fetch the two pawn bitboards once via board.pieces_mask(chess.PAWN, chess.WHITE) and board.pieces_mask(chess.PAWN, chess.BLACK). Inside the existing `for colour, sign` / `for piece_type` loop, when piece_type == chess.PAWN and the current square's _PASSED_MASK[colour] has no intersection with the enemy pawn bitboard, add sign * PASSED_BONUS[relative_rank] to score, where relative_rank is the pawn's rank from its own side's perspective (0..6, 6 == 7th rank) and PASSED_BONUS is a fixed closed-form tuple such as (0, 8, 14, 24, 42, 74, 122) centipawns. Apply the bonus flat (no phase scaling, no connected/protected/blockaded sub-terms) in this first version so the mechanism is tested cleanly. The quadratic-ish rank schedule gives the search a sharply rising reason to push a passer and to trade into endgames where its passers matter, which is the specific progress signal missing from the shuffling draws.
next_direction.rationale: The dominant retained failure mode across exp-0089 and exp-0090 is non-forced threefold-repetition draws from equal-or-better positions (29/64 in exp-0090), and multiple of those PGNs show the engine sitting on an extra passed pawn or a pawn majority in a rook ending and never advancing it. mobility (exp-0089, accepted) helped but is near-constant across moves in exactly those positions, so a second, orthogonal progress term is well motivated rather than redundant. Passed pawns are the canonical anti-draw progress heuristic, have never been tried in this project (absent from the registry and from both exhausted-mechanism lists), and are explicitly named as the next distinct term in the previous audit's own guardrails, which said that if the king-danger arena came back inconclusive the next step is passed pawns, then rook-on-open-file, then bishop pair. It is preferred over another king-attack term because exp-0090 just showed a static king-danger scalar does not move the needle, and preferred over rook-on-open-file / bishop pair because it targets the largest loss+draw column (endgame conversion) most directly. It is fully self-contained: precomputed masks plus a fixed coefficient tuple, no training pipeline, no new weights artifact, no change to how the trained model is used beyond an additive term far below its ~118-170 cp margin RMSE.
next_direction.guardrails: Keep the trained PSQT model and the accepted mobility term dominant: PASSED_BONUS must stay small enough that a typical position contributes well under ~0.4 pawn and a realistic worst case (two passers on the 6th/7th) stays under ~1.2 pawn, i.e. below the model's margin RMSE; do not let any single-position passed-pawn contribution approach a minor piece. NPS/leaf-cost budget: precompute the mask tuples once at import (import has a 60 s budget; this is trivial) and store them as module-level constants — no per-leaf object allocation beyond the two board.pieces_mask int fetches, no second legal-move generation, no board.push. exp-0090's stress showed the worst single move at the 120 s clock was 1.09 s against the 2.25 s ceiling and 0.044 s against 0.75 s at the 1 s clock, so the added work (a handful of int-AND / popcount-free emptiness tests per pawn) must keep leaf cost within roughly 1.3x. Use only documented python-chess API (chess.BB_FILES, chess.BB_RANKS, chess.square_rank, chess.square_file, chess.square_mirror, board.pieces_mask); never read library internals and never touch any path outside agent.py and weights/. No change to _budget_seconds, the iterative-deepening loop, move ordering, quiescence, or the transposition table. Must pass the full stress_time_left_ms grid (1 / 25 / 100 / 1000 / 120000) with required_failures 0 and init under 50 s, and must hold model-ablation minimum_strength_score >= 0.625 with >= 8 divergent moves at the 3 s ablation clock. If the paired arena is inconclusive, do NOT re-tune PASSED_BONUS, add phase scaling, or bolt on connected/protected/blockaded/candidate-passer sub-terms and call it a new experiment — move to the next distinct positional term (rook-on-open-file, then bishop pair). If a later term genuinely needs an offline-trained artifact (a positional-feature retrain of weights/model.json), flag that for the human rather than expanding candidate permissions.

audit_summary: Champion is agent.py at commit 4a0c988 (recorded as exp-0089): a mature PVS/LMR negamax with exchange-aware capture ordering/pruning quiescence, a depth-keyed transposition table, partial root-iteration salvage, a fast draw/terminal path, over a tapered learned piece-square model, plus the newly accepted fixed 3 cp/square net-mobility leaf term and a flat castling-rights scalar. exp-0090 (the previous audit's chosen next step) added a quadratic king-danger term — enemy-attacked squares of each king's one-step ring, capped, at -2.5*count^2 cp — and returned an inconclusive paired arena (18-29-17, score 0.508, CI [0.436, 0.580]), with CI, reliability stress (worst move 1.09 s vs 2.25 s ceiling) and model-ablation gates all clean and zero agent failures. That is one scientific non-improvement since the exp-0089 promotion (threshold is five), and it is not saturation: the search/ordering/quiescence/time direction is exhausted in its tested form, but the leaf-evaluation direction opened by exp-0089 has only had mobility (accepted) and king danger (inconclusive) reach the arena. Auditing exp-0090's retained games, the dominant failure mode is unchanged from exp-0089: non-forced threefold-repetition draws from equal-or-better positions (29 of 64 games), with PGNs showing aimless piece-shuffling in simplified positions, frequently while holding an extra passed pawn or a pawn majority that is never advanced; and all 17 losses are checkmates (middlegame king hunt plus several long endgame king hunts), which exp-0090 targeted directly without effect, indicating the mates are downstream of weak endgame conversion and passive defence rather than a missing static king-attack scalar. Decision: CONTINUE. Next experiment adds a cheap rank-scaled passed-pawn bonus to _model_evaluate using import-time precomputed front-span masks and a fixed closed-form coefficient tuple (e.g. (0,8,14,24,42,74,122) cp by relative rank), applied flat, reusing the existing pawn iteration with two board.pieces_mask fetches and no move generation. This is a materially new mechanism (no passed-pawn term has ever been tried; absent from both exhausted lists) and is the previous audit's explicitly pre-authorised fallback for an inconclusive king-danger arena. It keeps the trained model dominant (contribution well below the model's ~118-170 cp margin RMSE), holds one CPU / 2 GB / no network, and does not touch search, time management or protected surfaces. If it is inconclusive, rook-on-open-file then bishop pair remain, followed by flagging an offline positional-feature retrain of weights/model.json for the human before declaring scientific saturation. Uploading remains out of scope; the protected champion is newer and better supported than the live exp-0052-era upload.
